newsitem.title: UK: Branson says might float Virgin Rail a possibility.
newsitem.headline: Branson says might float Virgin Rail a possibility.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson said on Tuesday he was considering a share flotation for Virgin Rail, operator of two of Britain's regional passenger service networks.
Branson told reporters at a company news conference on Tuesday that he was considering a flotation as one option in helping to finance plans to acquire a major new fleet of trains for the company.
He said Virgin expected to issue within the next two weeks an invitation to tender for the 80 new trains worth 800 to 900 million pounds.

"It (a flotation) is nothing definite," Branson said. "We are going ahead to buy 80 new train sets...to the tune of 800 to 900 million pounds. There is a possibility that we may offer the public the opportunity to be involved in that process."

Branson was awarded a 15-year franchise to operate Britain's InterCity West Coast (ICWC) rail services between London and Scotland in February, adding to the Cross Country franchise awarded last November.
Virgin has already said the new trains were likely to be leased but a company spokesman said on Tuesday that an outright purchase for some of the trains was now being considered.
Virgin Group owns Virgin Rail in partnership with a group of financial institutions, including Bankers Trust New York Corp, Texas Pacific Group, J.P. Morgan and Electra Fleming.
The Guardian newspaper said on Tuesday that a flotation of Virgin Rail could value the firm at around 250 million pounds ($401.5 million).
